messages:
Maya Chen: Quick RFC follow-up: proposal to consolidate precision knobs into a single 'precision_profile' field that encodes an ordered candidate list + fallback policy. Want ops/telemetry/qa feedback before I update the RFC.

Jon Patel: Is this primarily SDK ergonomics or runtime simplification?

Maya Chen: Both. SDK: fewer surface area changes when adding new profiles. Runtime: centralized negotiation/fallback so we can reason about a single policy instead of many hardcoded paths.

Liam O'Connor: Concern: hiding choices could make debugging customer regressions harder. How would a tenant pin a specific precision?

Maya Chen: Profiles are explicit objects (name, version, candidate list). Customers can pin a specific profile or pass an override list. Example payload sketch: {"model":"rwd-13b","precision_profile":["fp8_aggr_v2","int8_v1","int4_safe"],"fallback":"quality_first"} (this is just a sketch).

Sasha Rivera: Telemetry needs: profile_name, profile_version, sample_rate, and a degradation_score tag on traces. Without structured fields we'll drown in ad-hoc logs.

Jon Patel: Add an 'explain' flag for canaries that returns decision reasons (e.g., kernel/kv/memory). Helps ops and support.

Liam O'Connor: KV-cache compatibility is tricky. If we change precision between requests we must avoid warming regressions or format mismatches. Two options: require profile families to be KV-compatible (small bitset on profile metadata) OR runtime keeps per-profile KV namespaces.

Maya Chen: Right. Per-profile namespaces are safest but memory-intensive. If we require families to be compatible, that constrains ops but saves memory.

Sasha Rivera: Suggest: make multi-namespace fallback opt-in per endpoint. Endpoints that need longctx can opt to pin a family; others can allow cross-profile fallbacks with separate namespaces. Ops also needs memory budgeting per namespace and an eviction policy.

eng-ml-bot: reminder: any profile storage change triggers DB migration + runtime feature-flag.

Jon Patel: Rollout plan: (1) internal canary with shadowed sampling and extensive traces, (2) small-customer canary with explain logs + quality hooks, (3) gradual ramp with regression-threshold gates based on degradation_score + user metrics to auto-rollback.

Maya Chen: SDK ergonomics: ship curated defaults like 'balanced', 'cost_saver', 'quality_first' mapping to vetted candidate lists. Power users can still provide explicit lists.

Liam O'Connor: Testing: add synthetic prompts targeting known failure modes (math, code, instruction-following, factual recall) into canary suites. Also add longctx warmup scenarios to detect KV regressions.

Sasha Rivera: Ops checklist to draft: telemetry schema changes, kv-namespace opt-in flags, memory budgeting per-profile, fallback latency budgets, and an incident playbook for precision regressions. I'll draft runbook.

Maya Chen: Action items: Jon - canary plan + rollback gates. Sasha - ops runbook + telemetry schema. Liam - test prompts + kv-compat heuristics. I'll update RFC with API sketch and compatibility matrix.

Jon Patel: Ping me when RFC updated; I'll add the canary playbook and failure thresholds.

Maya Chen: Will update by EOD and open a flagged PR if no blockers. :thumbsup:
